messages:
mara: opened a small PR to clarify the air-gapped installer flow and add a short KMS/HSM socket sanity checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4362 please skim for wording and any missing security notes.

linh: nice, i'll check the KMS bits. quick flag: please call out that customers using strict SELinux profiles may need an explicit file_contexts or `chcon` step for /var/run/hsm. suggested sentence: 'If SELinux is enforcing, set the socket context or consult your security team.'

mara: added a short SELinux callout. also included a tiny table for egress ports (customers kept asking for a single-line reference):

```
Target | Proto | Port(s) | Purpose
object-store | TCP | 443 | artifact fallback
ntp | UDP | 123 | time sync (chrony)
kube-cni | TCP | 30000-32767 | CNI ephemeral ports
```

akshay: QA note: please mark the CNI port range as 'common' but vendor-specific; some CNI plugins use different ranges. also add a line: 'test in staging VPC with identical routing before production'.

terry: on HSM health checks - include an explicit warning: do not paste PKCS#11 responses into tickets. for a liveness check, i usually run: `socat -T5 -d -d STDIO OPEN:/var/run/pkcs11.sock` then send a tiny init frame from the client. the doc should show expected non-sensitive output (OK/ERR codes) and an example that does NOT include keys.

linh: also add `pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/libykcs11.so -L` as a vendor-probe snippet and note that the module path differs by vendor and distro.

mara: added both socat and pkcs11-tool snippets + a short sentence to redact secrets before pasting support logs.

akshay: migration/helpdesk request: customers asked for a one-liner to verify offline bundle signature. consider including both sha256 and gpg examples: `sha256sum redwood-offline-1.3.0.tar.gz` and `gpg --verify redwood-offline-1.3.0.tar.gz.sig redwood-offline-1.3.0.tar.gz` with a link to our keyring doc.

mara: added the verification examples and linked to https://docs.redwood.ai/security/keyring (public).

terry: networking gotcha — some environments block ephemeral egress ranges via egress proxy. add a brief troubleshooting tip: if artifact fetches fail, try `curl -v --retry 3 https://objects.redwood.ai/...` from the node and check HTTP 200 vs 403/504. include sample curl output snippet.

linh: small security nit: don't instruct users to run `chown` on socket paths broadly. prefer `chgrp redwood && chmod 750` example and call out to least-privilege principle.

mara: switched the example to chgrp/chmod and left a note about vendor-managed sockets where chown isn't recommended.

docs-bot: Linkcheck: one internal link failed (https://intranet.redwood/private/keyrotate). @mara please replace or mark internal-only. Lint: docs lint OK.

mara: thanks docs-bot 44d replaced the internal link with the customer-facing key rotation guide and left an internal comment for the engineering runbook.

akshay: QA will double-check nftables -> iptables migration snippet tomorrow. i flagged a TODO in the PR to not ship it until QA signs off.

mara: perfect. i'll wait for QA on that piece and merge the rest. planning to push updates in ~45m and ping reviewers. if anyone wants to tidy wording before i merge, drop quick edits here. :rocket:
